freeze_record.weights: unchanged from the draft vector; the +/-20% weight-sensitivity suite in analysis/instrument_validation.py was executed against exactly these weights, and changing them would invalidate that reported result for no measured gain
freeze_record.items: 25 items retained; two artifact-level defects corrected before freezing (see fixes_at_freeze). Neither correction changes any number reported in the manuscript: score_vector() depends only on (dimension -> item-id map, weights, bands), and all three are byte-identical to the draft.
fixes_at_freeze: POLARITY. The draft declared one global response scale (Yes=0, No=1) while score_vector() consumes item values as risk directly. For 5 of 25 items 'Yes' is the risky answer (A1-A4 AI use/exposure; V1 cloud dependence), so a respondent applying the declared scale would score an AI-free firm at AI-exposure 100 and a heavy AI user at 0 - the dimension inverted. Every item now declares risk_when explicitly, and response_scale gives the mapping per polarity.

DOUBLE-BARREL / DOUBLE-COUNT. Draft D2 asked 'Are important business files backed up, and has restoring from backup been tested in the last year?' - two questions in one item, and its first clause duplicated H4 ('Are important files backed up?'). A firm without backups was therefore charged risk twice, across two separately weighted dimensions (hygiene .25 and data .10). D2 is now restore-testing only; backup existence is asked once, at H4.

response_scale.note: Each item declares risk_when. Gap items (risk_when='no') score risk when a control is ABSENT. Exposure items (risk_when='yes': A1, A2, A3, A4, V1) score risk when the exposure is PRESENT. A single global Yes=0 mapping inverts the AI-exposure dimension and V1.

scoring_note: DK scored 0.5 (neutral, flagged in output); dimension score = mean item risk x 100; total = weighted mean of dimension scores. analysis/instrument_validation.py consumes risk-coded response vectors (0/0.5/1) directly, so risk_when is the respondent-facing mapping that produces those vectors.

known_and_accepted: G3 (incident responsibilities written down) and I1 (written incident-response plan) both anchor to CSLS incidman. They are distinct constructs (accountability vs. runbook) and are retained as separate items; the shared anchor is a source-coverage limit, not a scoring duplication.
Reliability of the full 25-item battery remains open pending fielding - only the CSBS-mapped core (policy, training, insurance) admits a criterion test, as the coverage audit reports.
